transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I’m probably making more of it than it is, but I’ve been having some trouble at work. I’m a cashier, and sometimes at the register I sort of get stuck doing something that doesn’t really fit what’s happening—like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or just freezing with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is waiting.

It’s embarrassing. I try to move on and act normal, but last week it got me written up, so… I thought maybe I should come in and talk to someone. Is that the kind of thing you can help with?
Do you find yourself doing these repetitive actions, like tapping in a pattern, when you're not at work?

Not really that I’ve noticed at home… or, I mean, not in a way that’s caused trouble. The thing I came in for is mostly at the register—getting sort of stuck tapping the scanner in a pattern, or my hand just freezing over the cash drawer when someone’s waiting. It sounds strange when I say it out loud, but that’s what happened, and last week they wrote me up for it.
Do you feel anxious or overwhelmed in situations outside of your job?

Um… outside of work, I don’t think so. I mean, everybody gets stressed, right? But I wouldn’t say I feel especially anxious or overwhelmed in general. It’s mostly been noticeable at the register. If that makes sense.
Do you have any recurring thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?

I don’t think so… not in the way you mean, probably. I mean, I’ll worry about work after something awkward happens, but I wouldn’t say there’s one thought that keeps coming back and won’t leave me alone.

Is that what you’re asking? Like a thought I feel stuck on? Because I haven’t really noticed that, no.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations or tasks at work because of these episodes of getting stuck?

A little, I guess… I try not to make a big thing of it. At work I’m not exactly avoiding the register, because that’s my job, but I do find myself hoping someone else will handle certain parts when it’s busy, or I slow down getting back to the drawer because I’m worried I’ll freeze up again.

It’s gotten serious enough that I’m on a formal warning now, which is… embarrassing. And outside of shifts, I’ve kind of let other things slide too—friends, kayaking plans, calling family. I don’t mean to sound like I’m just making excuses. That’s just sort of what’s been happening.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with friends or family because of what's been going on with you?

Yeah… a bit, I guess. I wouldn’t say there’s been some big falling-out or anything, but I haven’t been keeping up with people like I used to.

I’ve let some plans slide—kayaking with friends, calling family back, that kind of thing. And with work… I’m on a formal warning now, so that’s been weighing on me too. I don’t know if that counts as relationship problems exactly, but I can tell I’m pulling back some.
Have you felt like your difficulties at work have significantly affected your overall well-being or daily life outside of your job?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but I think it has. Being on a formal warning at work now has kind of gotten in my head, and then when I’m not at work I’m not really doing the things I used to.

I’ve been letting friends drift, not following through on kayaking plans, not calling family back as much. It’s not like everything has fallen apart, but… it’s affected more than just the job, I guess. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
How distressing do you find these episodes of getting stuck at the register?

It’s… pretty distressing, honestly. I try to tell myself it’s just a small thing, like I’m just pausing or getting flustered, but when there’s a customer standing there and I’m stuck tapping the scanner in some pattern, or my hand is just hovering over the cash drawer and I can’t seem to move on… it feels awful.

And last week it got me written up, so I guess it’s not as small as I’d like it to be. I’m embarrassed even saying that. I don’t know if that answers it the right way.
Have you had to take any days off work due to these episodes of getting stuck at the register?

I haven’t really been taking days off, no… or at least not like calling out because of it.

It’s more that it’s catching up with me at work. I’m on a formal warning now, which is embarrassing to admit. And then outside my shifts I’ve sort of stopped keeping up with people—friends, kayaking plans, calling family back. So it’s affecting things, just not exactly as missed days, if that makes sense.
Are you finding it difficult to do everyday tasks outside of work because of your concerns about having these episodes at the register?

Yeah… I think so, to some extent. I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t function at all or anything, because I still get through the basics.

But since things got worse at work — especially being put on that formal warning — I’ve kind of pulled back outside of my shifts. I’m not keeping up with friends like I used to, I’ve let kayaking plans slide, and I don’t call my family back as much. It’s embarrassing, because it sounds small, but it has been affecting my day-to-day life more than I’d like. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you noticed any changes in how your friends and family interact with you since you started having these episodes at work?

A little, yeah… though I don’t know if it’s them changing so much as me sort of pulling back.

I haven’t been keeping up with friends the way I used to, and I’ve let kayaking plans kind of fall apart. I’m also not calling my family back as much. They’ve noticed, I think — or they check in and I don’t really have a good explanation.

I’m trying not to make a big dramatic thing of it, but with being on a formal warning at work now, I guess I’ve been embarrassed and more withdrawn. Does that make sense?
Have you felt like these episodes at work are affecting your ability to maintain relationships with your friends and family?

Yeah… I think it is, unfortunately. I don’t want to overstate it, because people still care and I’m not completely cut off or anything.

But since things at work got bad enough that I’m on a formal warning, I’ve been kind of embarrassed and I’ve pulled back. I’m not keeping up with friends the way I used to, I’ve let kayaking plans slide, and I don’t call my family back like I should.

So… yes, I guess it is affecting my relationships some. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you think you would have these episodes of getting stuck at the register if you were alone and didn't have to interact with customers?

I’m not totally sure… I want to say it would probably be less likely if I was alone, because the customer standing there makes it worse, or at least makes it more obvious.

But it’s not only the talking part. At the register I get sort of stuck in the action itself — like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or just freezing with my hand over the cash drawer when I should be moving. And then the customer is waiting, so it becomes… noticeable. That’s what got me written up last week.

So maybe if I were alone it wouldn’t happen the same way, or it wouldn’t matter as much. Is that answering it okay?
Do you think these episodes of getting stuck at the register would happen if you were working alone with no customers around?

I think… maybe it still could, yes. Maybe not as badly, because without a customer standing there it wouldn’t feel so exposed.

But the thing itself is more like I get caught in the action — tapping the scanner in this little pattern, or my hand just sort of hovering over the cash drawer when I’m supposed to be finishing the sale. When someone’s waiting, it becomes obvious and then I feel worse about it.

So if I were alone, I might still do it, but maybe it wouldn’t be such a problem. Does that make sense?
Do you think you would have these episodes if you were working at the register but there were no customers around and you didn't have to interact with anyone?

I think… yes, it probably could still happen, even if nobody was there. Maybe I wouldn’t call it an “episode” exactly, or maybe it wouldn’t look as bad, because no one would be waiting on me.

But the part that worries me is I get stuck doing something that doesn’t really fit the moment — like tapping the scanner in a certain pattern, or just freezing with my hand over the cash drawer when I should be moving on. With customers there it’s worse because they’re waiting, and that’s part of why I got written up last week.

So… yes, I think it could happen without the interaction, just maybe less noticeable. Is that what you’re asking?
Do you think your episodes of getting stuck at the register are more related to the pressure of performing your job tasks correctly or to the social interaction with customers?

I think it’s… maybe more the task itself than just the talking with customers. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but at the register I get caught doing things that don’t really fit, like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or I’ll just freeze with my hand over the cash drawer when I should be finishing.

The customer being there definitely adds pressure, because they’re waiting and then I feel embarrassed. But I think the getting stuck part is happening around the job action itself, not only because I’m interacting with them. Last week it got noticed enough that I was written up, so… that’s why I came in. Does that answer it the right way?
Do you think you would still get stuck at the register if you were doing a task that didn't involve interacting with customers, like counting inventory?

I think… yes, maybe it could still happen, even if it was something like inventory and nobody was talking to me. It’s not only the customer part, I guess.

At the register it’s just more obvious because I’ll get caught doing something that doesn’t really match what I’m supposed to be doing — like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or freezing with my hand over the cash drawer while someone is waiting. That’s what got me in trouble last week, the write-up.

So with inventory, maybe it wouldn’t be as noticeable or as embarrassing, but I’m not sure the “getting stuck” would completely go away. Does that make sense?
Do you think you would experience these episodes of getting stuck if you were performing a different job task that didn't involve using the register?

I think it might, yes… maybe not as obviously as at the register, but I don’t think it’s only the register itself.

The reason I came in is because at the register I keep sort of getting stuck doing things that don’t fit what I’m supposed to be doing right then — like tapping the scanner in a pattern, or just freezing with my hand over the cash drawer while the customer is waiting. And last week it got noticed enough that I was written up.

So if it was a different task, maybe it would be less embarrassing or less visible, but I’m not sure it would completely stop. Is that an okay way to put it?
Do you feel like you have to perform these repetitive actions, like tapping the scanner in a pattern, in order to prevent something bad from happening or to feel right?

I’m not sure I’d say it’s to stop something bad from happening, no. At least, I haven’t noticed a clear thought like, “If I don’t tap it, something will happen.”

It’s more like… I get caught in it, or it feels hard to move on for a second. Maybe there’s a feeling of needing it to be a certain way, but I don’t know if that’s the right explanation. I don’t want to overstate it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel like you need to perform these actions, like tapping the scanner in a pattern, in a very specific or symmetrical way?

Not really symmetrical, no… at least I don’t think of it that way. It’s more that I sort of get stuck doing it, like tapping the scanner in a pattern, and then I don’t move on when I should.

Or sometimes I just freeze, like with my hand over the cash drawer, even though the customer is standing there waiting. It sounds odd when I say it out loud. I don’t mean to make it a big thing, but that’s the kind of thing that got me written up last week. Is that answering what you mean?

So if it was a different task, maybe it would be less embarrassing or less visible, but I’m not sure it would completely stop. Is that an okay way to put it?
